quote: deliver to the Successor Servicer the Receivable Files and the accounts and records maintained by the Servicer. The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party
rationale:
Direction of ownership runs in our favour throughout. The Depositor "transfers and absolutely assigns to the Issuer... all of the Depositor's right, title and interest" in the Receivables and related Depositor Transferred Property (p0033, p0035), Cellco as Custodian holds the Receivable Files "for the benefit of the Issuer and the Indenture Trustee" (p0138) and they are constructively delivered to the Indenture Trustee as pledgee (p0142). Nothing of ours is assigned or licensed to Cellco, and no joint ownership is created — so the walk-away triggers are absent. On the flip side, Cellco retains only its own "processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications" (p0346), which is exactly the permitted Vendor-platform/generic-tools carve-out, and it remains obliged to deliver the Receivable Files and its servicing records to a Successor Servicer (p0346) and to the Indenture Trustee or successor custodian on termination of the custodial appointment, at its own expense (p0147). That combination of outright ownership of our asset files plus mandated return sits at or above the fallback.

Two sub-preferred points we note but do not flag: (i) access to and delivery of our own Receivable Files is expressed as "subject to" Cellco's/the Custodian's legal, regulatory, confidentiality, privacy and data protection policies (p0146, p0147, p0338), which are unilaterally set, and p0346 carries a catch-all for anything "otherwise restricted" by those policies — this qualifies the mechanics of return but cannot defeat our ownership; and (ii) there is no express perpetual licence-back to Cellco's servicing systems to aid a servicing transition. Neither is a material failure of the fallback under this rule, and the file-access point is better addressed under the records/audit rule than duplicated here.

quote: All other liability is expressly waived and released as a condition of, and consideration for, the execution of this Agreement by the Servicer or the Marketing Agent, as applicable. Each of the Servicer and the Marketing Agent, severally and not jointly, will be liable only for its own willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under this Agreement.
rationale: This securitization TSA contains no monetary limitation of liability at all, and that absence works in our favour. Cellco's exposure as Servicer/Marketing Agent (§ 6.2(a), p0283) and its indemnities to the Issuer, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee (§ 6.3(a), p0291-p0292) are unlimited in amount, so the indemnification, wilful misconduct, bad faith and gross negligence heads the playbook wants carved out of any cap in fact sit outside any cap. Our side is limited rather than exposed: the Depositor's liability is subject to the mirror-image standard in § 5.2(a) (p0243) and § 9.6 Limited Recourse (p0378) confines claims against the Depositor and the Issuer to the Depositor Transferred Property. The culpability standard is mutual as between the transaction parties, and p0469 bars punitive and consequential damages in arbitration for both sides, matching the mutual consequential-damages exclusion in the preferred position. None of the walk-away triggers is present — there is no Vendor-only cap, no sub-6-month cap, and no indemnities inside a cap. Noted but not flagged: there are no express confidentiality, data-protection or third-party IP carve-outs and no USD floor (the framework is uncapped, so a floor is unnecessary), and Cellco is answerable only for wilful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence rather than ordinary negligence — a market-standard servicer standard in ABS transactions and a sub-element short of preferred wording rather than a material failure. Proposing a monetary cap here would introduce a ceiling on our recovery against Cellco where none exists, so no redline.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: (a) Assignment. Except as stated in Sections 5.3, 7.4 and 7.6, this Agreement may not be assigned by the Depositor or the Servicer without the consent of the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee, the Certificateholders and the Noteholders of at least 66-2/3% of the Note Balance of the Controlling Class.
rationale: Section 10.2(a) imposes a symmetrical assignment restriction on the Depositor (our party) and the Servicer (Cellco), and expressly carves out Sections 5.3, 7.4 and 7.6. Section 5.3 gives us the full preferred carve-out: any Person into which the Depositor is merged or consolidated, resulting from such a merger, succeeding to the Depositor's business, or that is an Affiliate to whom the Depositor has assigned the Agreement automatically becomes the successor Depositor, with no counterparty consent required — only post-closing assumption/opinion/notice mechanics within fifteen Business Days. Section 7.6 mirrors this for the Servicer, so the arrangement is mutual. Cellco cannot exit: Section 7.1 (No Resignation) bars the Servicer from resigning unless it is legally unable to perform, and there is no change-of-control (or "deemed assignment") trigger anywhere in the document giving the Servicer a termination, re-pricing or fee-reset right on our change of control — searches for "change of control" and "may not assign" return no such provision. Two minor sub-elements fall short of the ideal preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: the residual consent standard for non-carve-out assignments is absolute rather than "not to be unreasonably withheld," and there is no express bar on assignment to a competitor. Neither is material here — the residual consent runs to the Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee, Certificateholders and 66-2/3% of the Controlling Class (structural noteholder protection benefiting the Issuer's capital structure, not counterparty leverage), and Section 7.4 independently controls who may succeed Cellco by requiring a $50,000,000-net-worth servicer acceptable to the Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee. The clause therefore meets the preferred position on its material terms; no redline warranted.

quote: The Issuer agrees that it shall not assert exclusive control over, or originate entitlement orders or instructions for the disposition of funds with respect to, the Cap Collateral Account unless the conditions for the exercise of its rights and remedies pursuant to the Cap Agreement are met
rationale: The agreement imposes no exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on our party, which meets the preferred position. This is a Transfer and Servicing Agreement for a securitization rather than a supply or procurement contract, so there is no purchasing relationship capable of being made exclusive. The only uses of "exclusive" are unrelated to dealing exclusivity: (i) "exclusive control" over the Cap Collateral Account in Section 9.10 (p0387-p0388), a standard secured-party account-control mechanic that operates in favor of the Issuer, and (ii) the "nonexclusive jurisdiction" submission in Section 10.6 (p0427), which preserves rather than restricts forum choice. Targeted searches for "sole supplier", "sole and exclusive provider", "all of its requirements", "shall not procure", "exclusivity", "sole source", and compete / third-party-provider restrictions returned no purchasing covenant binding the Issuer or the Depositor. Section 9.2's restriction on the Depositor transferring or encumbering the Depositor Transferred Property is an asset-conveyance protection benefiting the Issuer, not a restrictive covenant on our freedom to contract with other providers. No redline required.

This Agreement will terminate on the earlier to occur of (a) the date upon which the last remaining Receivable is paid in full, settled, sold or written off and any amounts received are applied and (b) the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.1 of the Trust Agreement.
rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum fee payable by our parties (the Issuer or the Depositor). Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "termination fee" and "premium" return no Customer-payable amounts, and Section 8.3 terminates the Agreement on the stated events without any exit payment to Cellco. The only premium-style amounts are Make-Whole Payments, which are noteholder economics on an Optional Redemption that the Class A Certificateholder (an Originator/Cellco affiliate) elects and funds (Sections 8.1(a), 8.2(a), and the Optional Acquisition/Redemption funding conditions in p0355 and p0362); the Clean-Up Redemption is expressly make-whole-free. The Article VI indemnities run from the Servicer/Marketing Agent to us, and the dispute-resolution provision bars punitive and consequential damages awards — both in our favor. This meets the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), so no redline is proposed.

quote: The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party, or provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies.
rationale:
This is a securitisation Transfer and Servicing Agreement, not a technology or procurement contract: Cellco does not supply us with any licensed product, software, deliverable or other IP, and correspondingly there is no affirmative licence grant clause anywhere in the document to test against the LICENSE rule. I checked every candidate and searched the full text — all "Grant"/"Granted" usages are security-interest grants in the Depositor Transferred Property (p0048, p0067, p0763), and all "license" usages other than p0346 are due-qualification representations about regulatory licences and approvals (p0234, p0259, p0272). Sections A-1 to A-41 are the definitions annex and contain no licence terms. The rule's material terms (affiliate/contractor scope, irrevocability, perpetuity for paid-up licences, successor transferability) therefore have nothing to attach to, so I am recording this as needs_review for a scoping decision rather than "missing" — inserting a licence grant into this instrument would not fit the transaction structure.

One related point is flagged for awareness rather than redline. The nearest IP-adjacent provision, Section 7.5(b) (p0346), runs the opposite way from the rule: it expressly negates any obligation on the Servicer to provide, license or assign its processes, models or servicing software to a Successor Servicer, so we and any Successor Servicer have no path to the Servicer's servicing platform on a transition. That is a genuine continuity exposure for the Issuer and the Noteholders, but it is the same commercial term the TRANSITION rule addresses (per the planner note), and it is settled market language in this sponsor's ABS programme. Consistent with the instruction not to flag one commercial term twice, I am not proposing a redline to p0346 here and defer it to TRANSITION. Note also that Section 7.6 (p0348) gives the Servicer, not us, succession/assignment rights, which is a counterparty-side benefit outside this rule's direction.

quote: petition a court of competent jurisdiction to appoint
rationale: This rule is satisfied at the preferred position by absence. The Agreement is a securitization Transfer and Servicing Agreement and contains no non-compete, exclusivity, field-of-use or territorial restriction binding our party (the Issuer, Verizon Owner Trust 2020-A, or the Depositor, Verizon ABS LLC). Targeted searches for "compete", "competing", "shall not engage", "field of use", "territor", "similar business" and "solicit" produced no restrictive-covenant language: the only matches for "compete" are the standard forum phrase "court of competent jurisdiction" (p0335, p0469). The "exclusiv" hits are unrelated — Section 9 concerns notices of exclusive control over the Cap Collateral Account (an account-control mechanic, not a business restriction), and Section 10.6 is a nonexclusive submission to jurisdiction. The "restrict" hits are ordinary no-contravention representations referring to pre-existing contractual restrictions, plus a Successor Servicer carve-out for information subject to third-party transfer or confidentiality restrictions, which limits a disclosure obligation rather than restricting what businesses we may operate. Nothing here constrains the products or services our party may buy, build or market, so no redline is warranted. Note for the file: because the Issuer and Depositor are special-purpose entities whose permitted activities are already narrowly circumscribed by their own organizational documents and the transaction documents, any future addition of a field-of-use or non-compete covenant should be resisted as unnecessary.

quote: Section 7.1 No Resignation. The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement.
rationale:
Neither side has a convenience exit, so the rule's two halves land in opposite directions and I am escalating rather than redlining.

Vendor side — better than preferred. § 7.1 (p0314) bars Cellco from resigning as Servicer at all except where it is legally unable to perform, and even then § 7.3 (p0329) requires it to keep performing until a Successor Servicer accepts, § 7.5 makes it cooperate on transition and bear transition expenses (p0347), and § 7.4(a)(ii) makes the Indenture Trustee automatic backstop servicer (p0335). The preferred position only asks that Vendor have "no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term"; this exceeds it.

Customer side — no convenience right. Removal is available only on a Servicer Termination Event, and then it is the Indenture Trustee acting at the direction of the Controlling Class, not the Issuer, who removes (§ 7.2(c), p0327). The Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid off (§ 8.3, p0363), well beyond 12 months. Read literally against the detection guidance, that is the walk-away trigger ("No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term").

Why I am not redlining. (1) The harm the rule protects against is absent: the Servicing Fee accrues per Collection Period in return for performing its obligations (p0134), there are no prepaid fees, no minimum-term commitment and no early-termination fee anywhere, so there is nothing to refund and no penalty to cap to 3 months' fees. (2) The missing right is structural, not a negotiated concession. Our party is a bankruptcy-remote SPE whose servicing rights are pledged to the Indenture Trustee for the Noteholders; vesting removal in the Trustee/Controlling Class is standard ABS architecture and rating-agency criteria. An Issuer 30-day convenience right would also be exercised through the Administrator, which is Cellco itself (see p0351, p0358, where even the optional exits require Administrator consent and sit with the Class A Certificateholder, defined at p0668 as the Originators or their designee), so the right would be illusory while cutting against our own Noteholders. Inserting it is disproportionate under the "existing bargain" carve-out.

Recommendation: confirm a playbook carve-out for securitization transfer-and-servicing agreements, or, if the deal team wants a lever, pursue it as an Indenture/Controlling-Class direction right rather than an Issuer convenience termination. Flagged as needs_review rather than compliant because the clause does not literally meet the fallback, and rather than deviation because the model redline would not benefit our party.

quote: Section 3.6 Review of Servicer's Records. The Servicer will maintain records and documents relating to its performance under this Agreement according to its customary business practices. Upon reasonable request not more than once during any calendar year, and with reasonable notice, the Servicer will give the Issuer, the Depositor, the Parent Support Provider, the Administrator, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee (or their representatives) access to the records and documents to conduct a review of the Servicer's performance under this Agreement.
rationale: The only audit/review rights in this Agreement run in our favour, not against us. Section 3.6 (p0131) gives the Issuer, Depositor and other transaction parties access to the Servicer's (Cellco's) records, and Section 6.7 (p0303 et seq.) requires the Servicer to deliver annual Regulation AB compliance assessments and a registered public accounting firm's attestation to us; under Section 3.9 (p0135) the Servicer bears its own expenses, including independent accountants' fees, so cost sits with the counterparty. There is no inspection, verification or audit right exercisable by Cellco against Verizon Owner Trust 2020-A or Verizon ABS LLC anywhere in the document (searches for "audit", "inspect", "examine" and "books and records" return nothing adverse), and no remote or direct access to our systems. Nothing to flag under this rule. Noted only (not a deviation, and in any event a limit on rights we hold): our Section 3.6 access is capped at once per calendar year on "reasonable notice", must be exercised by all parties simultaneously at the Servicer's offices, and is subject to the Servicer's own security, confidentiality, privacy and data-protection policies — customary for a securitisation servicing agreement, but it is the counterparty rather than an independent auditor that controls the conditions of access.

Law §§ 5-1401/5-1402) and bars any amendment changing the governing law away from New York, which matches the preferred position. Section 10.6 (p0427) submits the parties to SDNY and New York State courts sitting in New York, New York, with waiver of venue/forum non conveniens objections; jurisdiction is nonexclusive rather than exclusive, which is a minor departure from the preferred wording only and preserves optionality for us, so it is not redlined. The separate Section 11.2 mediation/binding arbitration track (p0450-p0469) is scope-limited to reacquisition/acquisition disputes over the Eligibility Representation, is elective at the Requesting Party's discretion (legal proceedings remain available), and is US-seated — any mediation or arbitration "will be held in New York, New York" (p0473) — so there is no foreign seat or mandatory foreign arbitration concern. quote: Section 8.3 Termination. This Agreement will terminate on the earlier to occur of (a) the date upon which the last remaining Receivable is paid in full, settled, sold or written off and any amounts received are applied and (b) the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.1 of the Trust Agreement.
rationale: The RENEWAL rule is not engaged by this Agreement. This is a transfer and servicing agreement within a securitization structure, and its term is event-based rather than a fixed term with renewals: under § 8.3 (p0363) the Agreement terminates automatically on the earlier of payoff/disposition of the last Receivable or termination of the Issuer under the Trust Agreement. Article VIII otherwise contains only Optional Acquisition/Clean-Up Redemption (§ 8.1) and Optional Redemption (§ 8.2) mechanics, which are exit rights, not extensions. Searches for "renew", "automatically" (only the successor-servicer appointment at p0335), extension/successive/initial-term language (only Receivable-level payment extensions and Upgrade Offers), and prior-notice windows return no auto-renewal trigger, no renewal term length, no non-renewal notice window, and no renewal price-uplift provision. There is therefore no renewal lock-in or pricing exposure to cap, and the self-terminating structure operates in our favour, so no redline is warranted. Noted for the record rather than flagged: because there is no renewal mechanic at all, the preferred elements (vendor reminder, opt-out notice, CPI/3% uplift cap) have nothing to attach to; if the parties later add a term-and-renewal construct, the preferred position should be applied then.

quote: (a) Cooperation on Termination. On its resignation or termination, the Servicer will cooperate with the Issuer, the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee and the Successor Servicer in effecting (i) the termination of its rights and obligations under this Agreement and (ii) an orderly transition of such rights and obligations to the Successor Servicer.
rationale: A usable exit/transition regime exists and, on its material terms, sits at or above the preferred position, so we do not redline it. Section 7.3 requires Cellco as Servicer to keep performing until a Successor Servicer accepts its engagement (or the date stated in the termination notice) — i.e. transition assistance of unlimited rather than 6-month duration — and Section 7.5(a) adds an express cooperation obligation for an orderly transition. Section 7.5(b) requires transfer of all funds and delivery of the Receivable Files and the accounts and records maintained by the Servicer to the Successor Servicer, and Section 3.10(f) requires the same of Cellco as Custodian; Section 7.5(c) puts all reasonable transition expenses on the resigning or terminated Servicer, which is better than the playbook's "then-current rates" and clearly benefits us. Minor sub-elements short of the model wording, noted but not flagged: delivery is "as soon as practicable" rather than within a fixed 30 days, no specified machine-readable format, and no deletion certification (unsurprising here, since the underlying obligor data is Cellco's own customer data that it must retain to service the wireless accounts). The p0346 carve-out (no obligation to license processes, models or servicing software, or to provide items restricted by confidentiality or privacy/data protection policies) narrows the assistance but does not defeat the mandatory delivery of the Receivable Files and records; p0338 and Exhibit A contemplate that information will in fact flow to a Successor Servicer that agrees to be bound by those policies. Nothing approaches the walk-away of no data return or immediate deletion.

quote: (a) General Servicing Obligations. The Servicer will manage, service, administer and collect on the Receivables with reasonable care using that degree of skill and attention that the Servicer exercises for all comparable device payment plan agreement receivables that it services for itself or others according to the Servicing Procedures.
rationale: Cellco (Servicer/Marketing Agent) gives express performance warranties in our favour that meet and in fact exceed the preferred position. Section 3.2(a) (p0082) imposes a workmanlike-equivalent performance standard (reasonable care and the degree of skill and attention used for its own comparable receivables, per the Servicing Procedures); Section 6.1(a) (p0257, p0268, p0269) contains express reps of compliance with all applicable Laws and material compliance with the Servicing Procedures, made as of the Closing Date and remade as of each Acquisition Date and expressly surviving transfer and pledge — i.e. no 12-month/90-day cut-off at all. There is a real remedy: breach of the Eligibility Representation triggers mandatory reacquisition/acquisition of the affected Receivable at the Acquisition Amount (p0072, p0073), the securitisation analogue of repair/replace/refund, backed by the asset representations review and dispute resolution machinery, and the security-interest reps survive termination and may not be waived (p0062). Crucially, there is no "AS IS" clause and no disclaimer of express or implied warranties anywhere in the document, so nothing swallows the express warranty. Two sub-elements are noted but not flagged: there is no conformance-to-documentation or malicious-code warranty (not applicable — this agreement procures servicing, not software or deliverables), and Section 6.2(a) limits the Servicer's and Marketing Agent's liability to willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, which is a limitation-of-liability point handled under that rule rather than a warranty failure (the reacquisition remedy operates independently of that fault standard).

verification.notes: The inserted clause (iii) completes every atomic element of the fallback: a Vendor-side IP infringement indemnity, the three customary exclusions (modification, combination, specification), all four remedies (procure/modify/replace/refund) and an express 3× annual fees super-cap. Preferred is not met: no express duty to defend, no affiliate coverage, and no breach-of-law or Vendor-caused data breach triggers; the drafter's locked target was fallback, so this is acceptable. Minimal: a single concise insertion filling an absent IP indemnity, with no rewrite of the existing willful misconduct/bad faith/gross negligence indemnities or the Proceedings mechanic; 'severally and not jointly' is necessary given two distinct indemnitors. Intent preserved: the existing notice/defence-assumption procedure in (b) applies to the new indemnity without contradiction, and the cap is expressly confined to clause (iii) so it does not dilute the existing uncapped indemnities.

ops.text: Insurance. The Servicer shall maintain throughout the term of this Agreement: (i) commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 in the aggregate; (ii) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $2,000,000; (iii) cyber liability insurance of not less than $5,000,000 covering the Servicer's processing of Obligor information; and (iv) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. The Servicer shall provide certificates of insurance to the Issuer and the Depositor on request.

proposal.summary: Insert a Servicer insurance covenant (CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' compensation, certificates) in Article X

quote: (i) The Servicer will indemnify the Issuer, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee (including in its capacity as Note Paying Agent), and their officers, directors, employees and agents (each, an "Indemnified Person") for all fees, expenses, losses, claims, actions, suits, damages and liabilities (including reasonable legal fees and expenses) resulting from the Servicer's (including in its capacity as Custodian) willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under the Transaction Documents
rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance covenant of any kind; the only "insurance" references are Obligor insurance premiums billed to wireless accounts (p0095) and FDIC deposit insurance in the "Qualified Institution" definition. Cellco, as Servicer/Custodian, collects payments, holds Receivable Files and processes Obligor account data, so it is a services provider that touches our data — walk-away territory when uninsured. The Servicer indemnity at p0291 reaches only willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence and provides no insured capacity. We therefore insert a short insurance covenant at the preferred limits as new Section 10.14 in Article X, now including the workers' compensation limb and without the self-insurance permission, post-termination tail or "at its own expense" wording that were extras beyond the preferred position.
